h1: Single-Family Rental Renovations for Portfolio Owners and Funds
lede: Owning one rental is a renovation project. Owning dozens or hundreds is a renovation program, and it needs different discipline: a finish standard every house meets, predictable scopes, reliable contractors in each market and reporting an asset manager can use. Genstone Construction renovates single-family rentals for individual portfolio owners, investment funds and REITs, from acquisition rehabs to capital projects on stabilized homes.

sections.h2: Treating rental renovation as a program
sections.body:
A single-family rental portfolio grows one house at a time, but it is managed as a whole. When every acquisition gets a different contractor, a different finish package and a different way of documenting the work, the portfolio becomes harder to maintain, harder to report on and harder to value. Faucets come from five manufacturers. Paint colors drift. Nobody can say with confidence what was replaced at which address or when.

Genstone approaches single-family rental work the way portfolio owners need it approached. Each renovation is still scoped to the individual house, because every house has its own condition and quirks. But the scopes are built on a shared standard, priced the same way, documented the same way and delivered through the same process regardless of which market the property sits in.

That consistency produces benefits beyond any single job. Maintenance teams stock fewer parts. Turn crews know what to expect. Asset managers can compare renovation costs across houses and markets without reconciling a dozen different bid formats. Lenders and auditors get a clear record of capital spending. And residents get a home that looks and works like the rest of the portfolio, which supports the brand many institutional owners are building.

This is the core of what we do for portfolio clients: apply the same scoping, field management, compliance and documentation discipline to the hundredth house as to the first. Our process, built around detailed scopes, a designated field manager and draws tied to completed work, was designed with exactly this kind of repeatable work in mind.

sections.h2: Building and holding a renovation standard
sections.body:
Most experienced rental owners eventually write down a specification standard, sometimes called a spec book or a rent-ready standard. It defines the materials, finishes, fixtures and quality bar every house must meet before it is leased. If you have one, we build every scope to it. If you do not, we can help you develop one from what is working across your existing homes.

A useful standard usually covers:

- Flooring type and color by room, typically a durable, waterproof plank or tile in place of carpet in most living areas.
- A paint palette and sheen for walls, trim, ceilings and doors, so touch-ups match across turns.
- Approved faucets, toilets, shower valves, lighting and door hardware, chosen for durability and parts availability.
- Cabinet and countertop options by price tier or submarket.
- Appliance packages with standard dimensions for quick replacement.
- Life-safety and habitability items every home must have before move-in.
- Exterior expectations: gutters, grading, landscaping cleanup, address numbers and entry lighting.

Some owners run more than one tier, such as a standard package for workforce housing and an upgraded package for higher-rent submarkets. That is common and sensible. The goal is not identical houses everywhere but a defined set of choices that are applied consistently.

Once the standard is set, holding it matters as much as writing it. Our field managers check finished work against the standard before final billing, and deviations are documented rather than quietly accepted. When a product is discontinued or unavailable in a market, we propose a substitute for your approval instead of letting each contractor choose.

sections.h2: Acquisition rehabs: from closing to first lease
sections.body:
Every day a newly acquired home sits between closing and its first lease is a day of carrying cost with no rent. For a portfolio buying steadily, the acquisition rehab is where the most money is won or lost, because it repeats with every purchase.

The process starts before the purchase. Our complimentary Pre-Offer Rehab Review estimates the anticipated renovation costs for a property you are evaluating and tells you whether the repairs and projected rental economics support the price. Portfolio buyers use it to underwrite deals with real repair numbers rather than rules of thumb, and to avoid properties whose hidden scope would push them outside the fund's return targets.

After closing, the estimator's findings become a detailed scope document and estimate with anticipated labor and materials, debris removal included, and a draw schedule. A designated field manager is assigned and the project moves into permitting, ordering and construction. Long-lead items are identified early so they do not hold up completion.

Acquisition rehabs often include more than finishes. Houses bought from long-term owner-occupants or estates may have original systems near the end of their service life. Houses bought from other investors may have deferred maintenance or past repairs that were not done to standard. Foreclosed homes may have freeze damage, mold or missing fixtures. Our estimators look for these conditions specifically so the scope reflects the real house.

The final step is a rent-ready handoff: punch list closed, home cleaned, standard verified and documentation complete, so leasing can begin without a second trip from maintenance.

Once a home is leased, renovation does not stop. It shifts from acquisition rehab to capital planning. Roofs age, heating and cooling equipment wears out, water heaters fail, exterior paint and siding weather, and driveways crack. Portfolio owners who plan for these replacements spend less over time than owners who wait for each failure to become an emergency.

Genstone handles capital projects on stabilized single-family rentals, including roof replacements, heating and cooling replacements, exterior repairs and painting, window replacements, plumbing repipes, electrical upgrades and foundation and drainage corrections. Each is scoped and priced with the same detail as an acquisition rehab and tracked with the same documentation.

Many capital projects happen while a resident lives in the home. That requires coordination: advance notice, clear scheduling, protecting the resident's belongings and keeping the home habitable throughout. Our field managers plan occupied work with those needs in mind. For repair work that is better suited to an ongoing maintenance relationship, Genstone Field Services provides occupied maintenance and repairs, along with inspections that can feed your capital plan.

Timing matters too. Some capital work is far easier to do at turnover, when the home is vacant. Flooring replacement, kitchen updates and interior paint are usually turn projects. Roofs, exterior paint and equipment replacements can often be done with a resident in place. We can help you decide which items to bundle with the next turn and which to schedule independently.

The result is a capital program with fewer surprises, better records of what was replaced and when, and homes that hold their condition over a long hold.

A rental home has obligations an owner-occupied home does not. Many cities and counties require rental registration or licensing, some conduct periodic rental inspections, and residents using housing choice vouchers bring their own inspection requirements. Insurance carriers and lenders also expect certain conditions to be met. A renovation that misses any of these can delay leasing or create liability.

Our scopes include life-safety and habitability items as standard work rather than optional extras. Typical items are smoke and carbon monoxide detectors where required, GFCI protection in wet locations, sound handrails and guards, working locks and egress from sleeping rooms, functional heat and hot water, adequate ventilation in baths and kitchens, and correction of trip hazards and damaged surfaces.

Older single-family homes add their own considerations. In homes built before 1978, renovation that disturbs painted surfaces must follow lead-safe work practices. Homes from the middle of the last century can contain asbestos in flooring, pipe insulation, siding or textured ceilings, which must be identified and handled appropriately before it is disturbed. Knob-and-tube wiring, older panel brands with known problems, galvanized supply lines and polybutylene piping are all common in older rental stock and can affect insurability.

Our team coordinates permits and inspections, verifies that assigned contractors carry appropriate insurance and meet applicable licensing requirements, and collects lien waivers. Genstone Field Services also offers code compliance and property care for homes that receive violations or need ongoing attention between renovations. The aim is a portfolio where every home can pass the inspections it is subject to.

Single-family rental portfolios are rarely concentrated in one city. A fund might own homes across several metros and states, each with its own building department, labor market and housing stock. Finding, vetting and managing a different contractor in every market is a large and often frustrating job for an asset management team.

Genstone operates on a national scale with local execution. We coordinate vetted, licensed and insured local contractors from a network of thousands, under the same process, standards and project management everywhere we work. Our footprint is strongest east of the Mississippi River, and our executive team brings more than 60 years of combined construction experience across REO, fix-and-flip and single-family remodeling.

For portfolio clients, reporting is part of the work, not an afterthought. Progress, documentation and milestones are visible without anyone needing to visit the property. Each project carries its own scope, estimate, draw schedule, photos, change records, permit documentation and lien waivers. That gives asset managers what they need to track renovation spending across the portfolio, report to investors and lenders, and compare cost and performance by market.

We can align our reporting with how your team already works, such as organizing projects by fund, market or acquisition batch, or matching your property identifiers. When questions come up, a designated field manager on each project and a consistent team of estimators and billing staff behind them mean you know whom to call.

Our clients include individual investors, mortgage servicers, REITs, investment funds, banks and other mortgage lenders, and we are a preferred contractor for Government-Sponsored Enterprises.

Portfolio relationships typically start with a conversation about what you own, where you are buying and how renovations are handled today. From there we agree on a renovation standard, a scoping and approval workflow, and the reporting you need. Some clients send every acquisition through us. Others start with one market or one type of work and expand from there.

Payment follows the same structure as every Genstone project. No upfront payment is required. Construction draws are tied to completed work, and final payment is due after the project is complete and you have approved it. Dumpster and debris costs are included in the estimate. Our billing team handles invoicing and documentation so your accounting team receives consistent records.

Completed work carries a one-year workmanship warranty. Damage caused by residents and normal wear and tear are not covered, which is one more reason we emphasize durable materials in rental scopes.

The Genstone Companies can support the rest of the ownership cycle as well. Genstone Financial offers DSCR rental loans, lines of credit and new construction loans. Genstone Insurance writes rental property, vacant property and multi-property portfolio coverage. Genstone Property Management handles leasing, resident screening, rent collection, maintenance coordination and owner reporting. Genstone Field Services covers preservation, inspections, occupied maintenance, turns and code compliance. Title Clearing & Escrow handles acquisitions and dispositions. Each is available independently.

To discuss a single-family rental renovation program, call (312) 429-2637 or send us a property or a list of properties for review.

faqs.q: Do you work with individual investors or only funds and REITs?
faqs.a: Both. Our clients include individual investors building rental portfolios as well as investment funds, REITs, mortgage servicers, banks and other lenders. The process is the same for all of them: detailed scopes, a designated field manager, coordinated permits and inspections, and draws tied to completed work. Larger clients typically add a written renovation standard and customized reporting, but an individual owner with a handful of homes benefits from the same consistency.

faqs.q: Can you build to our existing spec book?
faqs.a: Yes. If you have a written renovation or rent-ready standard, we build every scope to it, and our field managers check finished work against it before final billing. When a specified product is unavailable in a market, we propose a substitute for your approval. If you do not have a standard yet, we can help you develop one based on what is working in your existing homes.

faqs.q: Can you renovate homes while residents live in them?
faqs.a: Many capital projects, such as roof replacements, exterior painting and heating or cooling replacements, can be done with a resident in place. Our field managers plan occupied work with notice, scheduling and protection of the resident's belongings in mind. Work that is disruptive inside the home, like flooring or kitchen replacement, is usually better done at turnover. For ongoing repairs, Genstone Field Services provides occupied maintenance.

faqs.q: How do you handle homes in different states?
faqs.a: We coordinate vetted, licensed and insured local contractors from a network of thousands, under one process and standard everywhere we work. Each project has a designated field manager, and permits are handled through the local building department. Our footprint is strongest east of the Mississippi River. Reporting is consistent across markets, so your team can compare costs and progress without reconciling different contractors' formats.

faqs.q: What documentation do we receive for each home?
faqs.a: Each project includes the scope and estimate, the draw schedule, progress photos and milestones, any approved change records, permit and inspection documentation, and lien waivers. You can see progress and documentation without visiting the property. We can organize reporting by fund, market or acquisition batch, and match your property identifiers, so it fits the way your asset management team already tracks the portfolio.

faqs.q: Does the warranty cover resident damage?
faqs.a: No. Genstone provides a one-year workmanship warranty on completed work. Damage caused by residents and normal wear and tear are not covered. That is one reason we emphasize durable materials, accessible shutoffs and standard-size components in rental scopes. Those choices reduce the cost and disruption of repairs that fall outside the warranty, which matters more on a rental than on any other type of property.

faqs.q: Can Genstone also manage the homes after renovation?
faqs.a: Genstone Property Management, part of the Genstone Companies, offers rental marketing and leasing, resident screening, rent collection, maintenance coordination and owner reporting. Genstone Field Services handles turns, inspections and occupied maintenance. Using them is optional, and many portfolio clients keep their existing management in place while using Genstone Construction for renovations. When the same company group handles both, the handoff from rehab to leasing tends to be shorter.
